original.target_description: Experiment 1, immorality ratings of omission versus commission; within-person tennis tournament and witness scenarios. Main omission comparison reported as ordinal response counts, not as a numerical test statistic with its own p value.

n.sample_role: Participants contributing to the Experiment 1 main omission comparison; case 1 explicitly reports 37 out of 57.
n.exclusions: Responses justified by differences in intention were conservatively coded as no distinction, rather than excluded; no participant exclusion established for this main comparison.
n.location: Author manuscript printed pp. 7 and 9, sections 2.1 and 2.2
n.quote: In case 1, 37 out of 57 subjects (65%) rated each omission as less bad than either corresponding commission

es.location: Author manuscript printed pp. 9–10, section 2.2: no numerical test statistic for the main omission-versus-commission comparison

p.location: Author manuscript printed pp. 9–10, section 2.2: no p value for the main omission-versus-commission comparison

replication.target_description: Single replication experiment, Scenario 1 (The Tennis Tournament), immorality; omission versus pooled commission before/after, across harm outcomes; independent-samples t test.

n.sample_role: Participants in the replication experiment; all data included, with all conditions pooled for the Scenario 1 omission-versus-pooled-commission main effect.
n.exclusions: Supplementary p. 3 explicitly states no data exclusions. Table 2 has inconsistent Scenario 1 condition counts, so its individual cell Ns were not combined.
n.location: Manuscript p. 8, Participants and procedure; supplementary p. 3, Data exclusions
n.quote: A total of 313 American Amazon Mechanical Turk participants; There were no data exclusions. All data is included in the provided data.

es.location: Manuscript p. 30, Table 3; Scenario 1, Omission vs commission (pooled), Immorality row; metric identified in Table 4 note, p. 31

p.location: Manuscript p. 30, Table 3; Scenario 1, Omission vs commission (pooled), Immorality row

reported_success.location: Manuscript p. 14, Replication results: Morality and responsibility
reported_success.quote: We concluded a successful replication of the omission bias omission-commission asymmetry reported in the original study.

notes: Titles verified against supplied references. Original source is an author manuscript dated August 25, 2003 of the supplied 1991 work, retrieved as full PDF through web; local cache preserves relevant parsed excerpts only because direct download was blocked. The original main omission effect has descriptive counts but no printed test statistic/p pairing; chi-square values nearby concern cross-scenario correlation, legal/moral agreement or causality/morality association and were not substituted. Supplied page locators differ from the available manuscript pagination. Study 1 was interpreted as the first experiment and Scenario 1 as the replication target; the replication also reports Scenario 2 immorality (d = -0.47, t = -4.13, p < .001), which is not merged with Scenario 1. Replication Table 2 Scenario 1 cell Ns contain printed inconsistencies; total N and explicit no-exclusion statement used instead.
